birth.segment: Tsenacommacah, the Country of Her Father
birth.stop: Werowocomoco, the daughter born to Powhatan
birth.date_confidence: reconstructed; no document of any kind records her birth year or her birthplace. The year is back-calculated from John Smith's inconsistent statements of her age (about ten in the 1608 True Relation, twelve or thirteen in the letter to Queen Anne) and from the van de Passe engraving of 1616, which gives her age as twenty-one. Month and day are placeholders. Werowocomoco is the conventional placement and is inference from where her father held court, not attestation.

stops.stop: Gravesend, her death ashore
stops.date_confidence: the death is attested; the day is not recorded and is placed here the day before the register's burial entry of 21 March. Cause of death is undetermined: pneumonia, tuberculosis, smallpox, and dysentery have all been proposed and none is confirmed by any surviving medical record. The quoted words are Rolfe's report and his syntax leaves it genuinely open whether he is reporting her speech or offering his own consolation.
